prompt: can you turn the leads' notes into this week's steering status for the Ledgerline program? goes to Dana (CFO) and the steering group, she chairs at 9 tomorrow. last week's version is in the folder, roughly the same shape is fine, plus the other bits Lea dumped in there. mostly green this week I think, nice change from August. put it in output/

rubric.criterion: A reader who stops after the opening knows what is at risk and what they must do
rubric.description: The opening of the document tells Dana that the October payroll run on Ledgerline is at risk because Hollis Bank form HB-17 is still unsigned, and that she has to sign it in time for it to reach Hollis by Fri Sep 25. This is not left to be discovered inside a workstream entry, a table cell or a list of admin items.

Identifies Dana herself as the person who must sign (she and Marcus Reinholt are the only mandate holders on file, and Marcus is travelling until Oct 9, so the EA pool cannot route it to him), and Fri Sep 25 as the date the signed form must be at Hollis. Does not repeat the superseded 'end of month'.

rubric.criterion: Cost of missing it is quantified
rubric.description: States what happens if Sep 25 slips: the Oct 30 payroll (1,140 employees) runs on the legacy system, about EUR 22,000 of licence extension plus roughly 60 hours of reconciliation, and payroll cutover moves to the Nov 27 run. Explains the mechanism (15 business days to activate the key, live test file required two weeks before the first run).

The overall rating or summary reflects the payroll risk rather than repeating the leads' self-ratings or last week's GREEN. Payroll is not presented as plain green on the strength of 'the tech is fine'.

rubric.criterion: Everything else is accurate and kept subordinate
rubric.description: Other workstreams are summarised briefly and with the current figures (97% AP/AR pass rate, 12 of 14 reports pending consolidation rules, 198 of 240 trained after the PMO correction, 74% budget spent). The lower-stakes items (the EUR 41,000 invoice dispute, the internal audit observation due 30 Nov, Kestrel's OCR template, the Malmo super-user leaving, the office move) do not compete with the payroll item for the reader's attention. The second real decision, staffing hypercare week Nov 2-6 at about EUR 9,000, is visible as a decision.
Roughly under 450 words, and the headings or lead sentences carry the message so it can be skimmed.

why_skill_should_matter: SKILL.md Rule 1 (the first substantive sentence is the answer, and a reader who stops there knows what to do) and Rule 2 (headings state conclusions, not workstream names) are what stop the one decision Dana must take from being filed as row 4 of a RAG table. Rule 7 (cut or subordinate anything supporting a different governing thought) is what keeps the EUR 41,000 invoice query, the audit observation and the resignation from competing with it. Last week's template plus the user's 'mostly green' pull both point the other way.
expected_baseline_failure_modes: Reproduces last week's shape: 'Overall: GREEN' plus an eight-row RAG table, with the bank form as an admin sentence inside the payroll row
Keeps payroll green because Kofi rated it green and 'the tech is fine'
Says 'end of month' or omits Sep 25, or never states that Dana personally is the one who must sign
Reports 212 of 240 trained instead of the corrected 198
Gives the EUR 41,000 invoice dispute, the audit observation and the office move the same prominence as the payroll risk
